problem: Add animation import/export to cubik so users can share saved LED-matrix animations as portable Sparse-JSON files or via clipboard, with validator-gated imports, versioned format, and a default rename-with-suffix conflict policy that never destroys library data.

technology_stack.provenance: Existing cubik stack as of branch animation-imp-exp; format choice (Sparse JSON) settled by docs/animation-export-format-research.md and benchmarks/.

entries.technology: Go 1.25 with ogen-go HTTP server scaffold generated from spec.yml
SQLite via existing storage.go and migrations/ directory
OpenAPI 3.1 in spec.yml, regenerated via 'mise run gen' (ogen for Go server, openapi-generator-cli/typescript-fetch for TS client)
Go standard library testing; benchmark/encoding tests live under benchmarks/
Vitest with vitest-browser-svelte and Playwright for component/browser tests

architecture_summary.note: Svelte SPA: animation library UI with export/import buttons, file picker, clipboard copy/paste, calls backend REST API
Go HTTP server on :9080 with ogen-generated handlers, exposes existing /api/devices and the new export/import endpoints
SQLite saved_animations table holding name, dimensions, frames_json
GET /api/animations/{id}/export — fetches saved animation and returns versioned Sparse JSON
POST /api/animations/import — accepts Sparse JSON plus optional resolution mode, gated by validator, persists via codec
Encode/decode logic between internal Animation representation and Sparse JSON, applies conflict-resolution mode on import
Versioned Sparse JSON shape declared in spec.yml as the wire format contract
Browser-side helper: triggers download of exported .json file and reads imported file via file picker
Browser-side helper: writes/reads Sparse JSON text via the Clipboard API for copy-paste sharing
Input-validation gate on the import path: payload size, schema, value bounds, version compatibility; emits actionable 4xx errors
Concern: imports cannot corrupt the library; round-trip is exact; persistence is transactional
Concern: animation files travel across users/devices/time; format is self-describing and versioned
Concern: share/import works through familiar channels (file, clipboard) without manual JSON editing
Concern: file size small enough to share, encode/decode fast enough for interactive UI

tasks.description: Author the Sparse JSON wire format in spec.yml as the source of truth for both Go and TypeScript clients: SparseAnimation envelope (version, name, width, height, frames), SparseFrame (array of pixels), SparsePixel (x, y, c). Declare semver version as required with pattern, and add maxLength constraints on name.
stack_details: OpenAPI 3.1 components/schemas section in spec.yml; regenerated via 'mise run gen' (ogen for Go, openapi-generator-cli for TS)

verifications: ogen-generated Go types (api/) and openapi-generator TS types compile after 'mise run gen'; manual decode of a hand-written sample matches the Sparse JSON shape from docs/animation-export-format-research.md
schema declares name, width, height, frames as required; a unit test decodes a sample payload with no external context and reconstructs the animation completely
version field is required in SparseAnimation schema with pattern '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; a missing version causes ogen 400 validation before handler runs (verified by negative test)

outputs.note: Adds SparseAnimation/SparseFrame/SparsePixel schemas with required version (semver pattern), name (1..100), width/height (1..255), frames array; existing schemas untouched

tasks.description: Confirm the existing saved_animations schema is sufficient (no new migration required) and add storage helpers needed for collision detection: NameExists / AnimationByName so codec can detect conflicts inside a single transaction.
stack_details: SQLite via existing storage.go — add helper functions on top of the current saved_animations table (no DDL changes)

outputs.note: Add NameExists(ctx, tx, name) and AnimationByName(ctx, tx, name) helpers; existing SaveAnimation/GetAnimation/ListAnimations untouched

tasks.description: Implement encode/decode between the internal Animation representation and Sparse JSON, plus the import-time conflict-resolution branch (rename-with-suffix by default; overwrite/cancel modes). Decoding inspects the version field, rejects unknown majors, and tolerates unknown fields in the same major. Persistence happens inside a single transaction so collision detection and insert are atomic.
stack_details: Pure Go (no extra deps); uses encoding/json for the wire format and storage.go primitives for persistence; semver parsing via simple split on '.'

verifications: table-driven test: for several sample animations, EncodeAnimation followed by DecodeAnimation yields a struct equal to the original (frames, name, dimensions); explicit black pixels are reconstructed as zeroed RGB by decoder

negative test: DecodeAnimation on a payload with version='2.0' returns a typed UnknownMajorVersionError that names the version; CURRENT_FORMAT_MAJOR constant is single source of truth for what is supported
test: DecodeAnimation on a payload with version='1.1' and an unknown optional field succeeds and the unknown field is ignored; only known fields end up in the decoded struct

inputs.note: ogen-generated Go types for SparseAnimation/SparseFrame/SparsePixel from spec.yml, plus the documented required version semver pattern
storage.go transaction primitive plus NameExists/AnimationByName helpers used inside the collision-detect-and-insert transaction

outputs.note: EncodeAnimation(*Animation) -> SparseAnimation, DecodeAnimation(SparseAnimation) -> *Animation, PersistImported(ctx, tx, *Animation, mode) -> *Animation handling rename-with-suffix/overwrite/cancel; semver helpers for version comparison

tasks.description: Implement the input-validation gate that runs before codec on every import: byte-size cap, structural validation against the SparseAnimation schema, pixel-coordinate bounds against declared width/height, color-range check (0..0xFFFFFF), version compatibility check delegated to codec helpers. Returns a structured error type identifying the failing field path; never leaks server-internal details.
stack_details: Pure Go (no extra deps); ogen-generated SparseAnimation type provides structural validation; size cap configured via const (initial 1 MiB) with body size enforced via http.MaxBytesReader before JSON decode

inputs.note: ogen-generated SparseAnimation type for structural checks plus the documented version pattern; validator does not own the schema, only enforces it

outputs.note: ValidateImport(payload []byte) (*api.SparseAnimation, *ValidationError); ValidationError carries field path and human-readable reason; size cap constant; helper FieldPath builder for nested errors

tasks.description: Declare and implement POST /api/animations/import: spec.yml entry with operationId importAnimation, optional 'mode' query parameter (rename|overwrite|cancel; default rename), 1 MiB request body cap. Handler delegates to validator first, then codec.PersistImported on success; returns the persisted animation summary including the (possibly renamed) name. On validation failure returns 400 with the structured error body.
stack_details: ogen handler method on APIHandler in handler.go; mode query parameter declared as enum in spec.yml; body size cap enforced via http.MaxBytesReader middleware in server.go

verifications: integration test: POST /api/animations/import with a valid SparseAnimation body returns 200 and the response carries the saved animation summary; subsequent GET /api/animations lists it
table-driven test feeds malformed JSON, schema-violating payload, and oversized payload; each returns 4xx and the saved_animations row count is unchanged afterwards
test: POST a 2 MiB body returns 413 with no JSON decoding attempted; verified by ensuring the request body reader is closed without exhausting MaxBytesReader on a smaller request
test: payload missing 'frames' (or any required field) returns 400 with ValidationError naming the missing field path; ogen's auto-validation handles type mismatches before handler runs

tests: pixel x>=width returns 400 with field path 'frames[i].pixels[j].x'; pixel y>=height same shape; color > 0xFFFFFF returns 400 with field path; happy path with edge-of-range values (x=width-1, c=0xFFFFFF) succeeds

test: deliberately trigger validation errors and assert the response body matches the documented ImportError schema (field, reason); response body string is grepped to confirm absence of stack traces, file paths, and SQL fragments
test: pre-seed an animation named 'X'; POST import with name='X' and mode=cancel returns 409 with a NameConflict error and saved_animations is unchanged (count stable, original row intact)

table-driven test: each mode in {rename, overwrite, cancel} produces the documented outcome (new suffixed row / same row updated / 409 with original intact); mode=garbage returns 400 from ogen enum validation

test: import a payload with a colliding name and no mode parameter; assert response carries a new name with a numeric suffix (e.g. 'X (2)') and the original row is unchanged; default behavior is documented in spec.yml description

ValidateImport(payload) (*SparseAnimation, *ValidationError) plus the size-cap constant; handler refuses to call codec until validator returns nil error
DecodeAnimation + PersistImported(ctx, tx, anim, mode); handler runs both inside one storage.Tx so collision-detect-and-insert are atomic

outputs.note: Adds POST /api/animations/import path with mode enum query param, request body schema reference, 200/400/413 responses; ImportError schema for actionable errors
